findings: V8 base::Mutex embeds absl::Mutex and delegates Lock/Unlock/TryLock; level is DEBUG-only. MutexGuard is movable pointer RAII and clears the moved-from pointer. Node uv_mutex_t is a distinct original owner.
PID is the actual platform PID converted to int. TID is the platform ID converted to int, cached in static thread_local int at the actual OS wrapper.

Windows x64 ThreadTicks uses QueryThreadCycleTime and independently calibrated TSC frequency, not QueryPerformanceFrequency directly; initial evaluation under 50ms returns an empty zero value. It temporarily raises/restores thread priority during calibration. Windows ARM64 uses user FILETIME only. Linux/POSIX uses CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID with the original fatal clock failure path.

TimeTicks and ThreadTicks remain separate. Windows TimeTicks chooses QPC only after frequency and nonstop-TSC checks; otherwise rollover-protected timeGetTime. Non-Windows TimeTicks has its original platform-specific microsecond conversion and +1.
Controller samples CPU timestamp before recording_ admission. Source does not add an IsSupported or WaitUntilInitialized call there.

Node selected features enable V8_ENABLE_SYSTEM_INSTRUMENTATION on win and mac, disable elsewhere; Perfetto defaults false. libplatform admits actual platform Recorder sources. This is compile admission, not evidence that a system writer is instantiated.
The acquired V8/Node source files and selected exact operations are immutable full files. No generic mutex/time shim is qualified by this proof.
